chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and al-Fuḍayl, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:

Whenever you become certain, or doubt during the time of a salat (prayer), that you have not performed it—or, at the time of its passing, that you did perform it—then if you doubt after the time of missing it has gone out, a barrier has entered, so there is no repetition upon you due to doubt unless you become certain. But if you become certain, then you must repeat it by performing it, in whatever state you may be.

key_terms.اسْتَيْقَنْتَ: you became certain; attaining certainty about whether the salat (prayer) was performed
key_terms.تُصَلِّيَهَا: that you perform it; carrying out the missed salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَائِلٌ: a barrier; a separating factor after the prayer time has passed
key_terms.شَكَكْتَ: you doubted; uncertainty regarding performance of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْفَوْتِ: the time of lapse; when the prayer time has passed and the salat (prayer) is considered missed
key_terms.وَقْتِ صَلَاةٍ: the time of a salat (prayer); the legally designated period for its performance

ai.seo_question: If I doubt after the prayer time has passed whether I performed the salat (prayer), do I have to repeat it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about doubt and certainty regarding whether a salat (prayer) was performed within its time. Mere doubt after the time has passed does not require repetition, but certainty that it was missed does require that it be performed again. It reflects the juristic distinction between doubt and certainty in acts of worship.
